results.hypothesis: To evaluate whether gradient-boosted decision trees (XGBoost, LightGBM) maintain or improve their accuracy advantage over neural networks on large-scale tabular credit-risk datasets, and whether this advantage plateaus or diminishes as dataset size increases beyond 1 million records.

results.success_criteria: If gradient boosting models maintain higher accuracy than neural networks across all dataset sizes, and if their advantage decreases or plateaus at 1M records, then the hypothesis is supported.
